question: What is the primary goal of patient safety measures in a hospital?

options.A: To prevent harm and medical errors during care
options.B: To lower the cost of purchasing medical drugs
options.C: To speed up the discharge process for doctors
options.D: To reduce the total number of hospital beds

explanation: Patient safety is centered entirely on stopping avoidable injuries and medical mistakes before they harm the person receiving treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why is nurse safety considered just as important as patient safety?

options.A: Healthy and protected nurses provide better care and prevent errors
options.B: Hospital management is only legally liable for nurse injuries
options.C: Patients cannot recover unless nurses take daily rest breaks
options.D: Nurses pay for hospital equipment out of their own salaries

explanation: When nurses are safe from burnout, injuries, and infections, they remain alert and capable of delivering high-quality, error-free care to patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is a major environmental hazard in hospital corridors?
explanation: Leaving equipment or boxes in hospital hallways creates clear tripping hazards for staff, visitors, and vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h2)

question: A nurse notices a frayed electrical cord on an infusion pump. What is the immediate action to take?

options.A: Leave a sticky note on the screen and use it for one patient
options.B: Remove the pump from service and tag it for repair
options.C: Wrap the frayed area tightly with standard office tape
options.D: Plug it into a different wall socket to test the current

explanation: Frayed electrical cords pose severe shock and fire risks, so faulty equipment must be immediately taken out of use and labeled for biomedical maintenance. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of hospital infections?
explanation: Frequent and thorough handwashing or alcohol rubbing removes transient microorganisms and stops them from passing between patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: Why must used needles be placed immediately into a hard, puncture-proof container?

options.A: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries to staff
options.B: To prevent patients from stealing the metal needles
options.C: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to burn them
options.D: To comply with hospital fashion and sorting rules

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps containers stop sharp needles from poking through soft plastic bags and injuring nurses or housekeepers. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which group of hospitalized individuals faces the highest risk for severe falls?
explanation: Aging bodies often experience muscle weakness, balance issues, and dizziness from medications, making older adults much more vulnerable to falls. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: An older adult patient admitted with dizziness tries to get out of bed unassisted to use the bathroom. What is the best immediate preventive action?

options.A: Tie the patient's hands securely to the bed railings
options.B: Turn off the room lights so the patient stays in bed to sleep
options.C: Scold the patient for trying to walk without asking first
options.D: Respond quickly to the call bell and assist the patient to walk

explanation: Answering call lights promptly and providing physical support during movement keeps unsteady patients safe without resorting to unsafe restraints. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h4)

question: How many unique patient identifiers must a nurse check before giving any medication?
explanation: Checking two unique identifiers, such as the patient's full name and hospital number, ensures the medicine goes to the right person. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is an independent double-check required for high-alert medications like insulin?

options.A: Hospital computers will crash if only one nurse logs into the system
options.B: These drugs carry a high risk of causing serious patient harm if misused
options.C: Double-checking makes the nursing shift go by much faster
options.D: Pharmacy departments refuse to dispense them to a single nurse

explanation: High-alert medications have a narrow safety margin, meaning even a small dosing mistake can lead to catastrophic patient outcomes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h5)

question: What are the three core principles of radiation safety?
explanation: Limiting exposure time, increasing distance from the source, and using physical shielding protect workers from harmful radiation. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of wearing a personal dosimeter badge in a radiology department?

options.A: To prove to patients that the diagnostic equipment is clean
options.B: To block radioactive waves from entering the nurse's chest
options.C: To grant the nurse emergency access to locked X-ray rooms
options.D: To measure the accumulated amount of radiation exposure over time

explanation: Dosimeter badges record occupational radiation doses, alerting staff if their exposure levels begin to approach unsafe limits. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty disaster?

options.A: To collect insurance and payment details from victims
options.B: To sort and prioritize patients based on injury severity
options.C: To discharge healthy staff members so they can go home
options.D: To clean and disinfect the emergency room floors

explanation: Triage allows medical personnel to quickly identify and treat those with life-threatening injuries first when resources are limited. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why do healthcare facilities conduct regular fire and disaster drills?

options.A: To frighten new students so they stay alert on the ward
options.B: To ensure staff can respond calmly and efficiently during an actual crisis
options.C: To give the maintenance team a chance to test the lights
options.D: To fulfill insurance rules without teaching staff any real skills

explanation: Regular practice builds muscle memory and confidence so healthcare workers follow evacuation and safety steps automatically during a real emergency. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h7)

question: Where should a nurse document an accidental medication mishap or patient fall?

options.A: Inside the personal diary of the ward manager
options.B: On the front cover of the patient's bed chart
options.C: In a public text message sent to local news stations
options.D: On a separate institutional incident report form

explanation: Incident reports are kept separate from the official medical record to track safety data and improve hospital systems. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why is it important to report near-misses even though no patient was actually harmed?

options.A: To give the nursing supervisor extra paperwork to file away
options.B: To punish the staff member who almost made the mistake
options.C: To help identify hidden system weaknesses before a real injury happens
options.D: To increase the financial billing charges for the patient

explanation: Analyzing near-misses uncovers dangerous process flaws, allowing the hospital to fix them before a patient suffers actual harm. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h8)
